name: MonarchColumnsBlock
title: ColumnsBlock
wrapsNative: A custom Layout that places the children side by side like an HStack, top-aligned, and stacks them like a VStack below 480 points or at the accessibility text sizes
summary: Two or three side-by-side columns inside a document, which stack into one column on narrow screens.
whenToUse: When two or three short pieces of document content read better next to each other: a comparison, an image beside its notes.
whenNotToUse: For screen layout around a document (a list beside a detail), use NavigationSplitView or MonarchResizablePanels when the person resizes the split. For data in rows and columns, use a table (MonarchTableBlock in a document). For a grid of equal items, use LazyVGrid.

options.name: ratio
options.description: The share of the width for the first of two columns, kept between 0.2 and 0.8 (0.5 when not finite). Three or more columns are equal.

options.name: content
options.description: The columns, one child view each. A column of several views goes in a VStack.

states.name: side by side
states.description: At 480 points wide or more, the columns sit next to each other with a 24-point gap, top-aligned.

states.name: stacked
states.description: Below 480 points, and at the accessibility text sizes, the columns stack in order with a 12-point gap.

appearance: No surface or colour of its own: only spacing from the space tokens. The columns' content brings its own colours.
platformNotes: The web ColumnsBlock is both a static component and a Tiptap editor node with a keyboard and pointer resize handle that writes the ratio into the document. iOS has no Tiptap document model, so only the static block is offered; for a split the person resizes, use MonarchResizablePanels. The web stacks with a container query at 30rem; iOS uses the width the layout is offered, 480 points. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The block is a container: VoiceOver reads the first column completely, then the next, in order.
At the accessibility text sizes the columns stack so text keeps a readable width.
Columns are placed from the leading edge, so the first column is on the right in right-to-left languages.
edgeCases: A column taller than the others sets the block's height; the others stay at the top.
Inside a horizontal ScrollView, which offers no width, the block assumes 480 points and lays the columns side by side.

examples.title: On a page
Three equal columns of several views each
